name: Zeabur

modes.label: Bring or buy server; compute separately billed
modes.commit_note: Servers are billed monthly at a fixed rate and auto-renew until cancelled; sizes.hour = month/730.
modes.note: Fixed-price monthly servers resold by Zeabur (Tencent Lighthouse, Aliyun SWAS, DigitalOcean, Linode, Hetzner), cheapest plan per vCPU/RAM shape from the live catalog (api.zeabur.com dedicatedServerPlans, as used by zeabur.com/pricing); hour = monthly price/730. Prices vary by provider and city; US and EU entries are both listed (city in name). A Zeabur plan fee is charged on top.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: CONFLICT: pricing page says buying a server needs a paid plan ('Paid subscription required'), docs/server FAQ says 'No, you do not need a subscription plan to use a server'. Refund policy: after downgrading to Free, 'your currently deployed containerized services will be automatically suspended by the system'. Free plan is non-commercial only (Fair Use).

caveats: Runtime server prices vary by selected marketplace provider and location.
14-day Dev/Pro trial is promotional; no permanent free compute inferred.
Unknowns remain null, not free; generic infrastructure modes are opt-in alt.
Worked example assumes resources are released between active windows unless a retained-instance scenario is explicitly discussed.
VAT basis: Unknown: reviewed pricing source does not explicitly establish VAT/tax inclusion.
Residency: Server marketplace lets users choose provider and city; selection determines runtime location. Control-plane/support residency not established.

Server billing mechanics: monthly prepaid, auto-renew charged from balance; on failed renewal the server is powered off (1 day after expiry for AWS Lightsail/GCP/Hetzner/Linode/DO; at expiry for Tencent/Aliyun/Volcengine) and deleted after ~7 / ~15 days. Upgrades are one-way (no downgrade). Refunds: prorated, as Zeabur credits; Tencent/Aliyun/Volcengine only one unconditional refund per account. Prepaid credits non-refundable. Zeabur resells Hetzner ABOVE Hetzner list (cpx32 $48 vs originalPrice $42.99) but Tencent/Aliyun/Linode below list.
Shared (usage-billed) cluster deprecated: no new projects; existing shared-cluster projects stopped accepting new services on 2026-04-01. All compute is now Servers (fixed monthly) or BYO servers.

Plan limits (pricing page): manageable own (BYO) servers Free 1 / Dev 3 / Pro 10 / Team unlimited; build CI 2C4G (Free/Dev) or 4C8G (Pro/Team); log retention 48h/7d/30d/90d. Dev and Pro: 14-day free trial ('$0 First 14 days free'). Team $79 = 3 seats, +$24/seat. Plan fees are on top of server costs.

fleet.verification: Free plan requires no credit card.
fleet.notes: Plan comparison distinguishes managed services, user-hosted servers and AI credits. No verified universal fresh-account machine/vCPU/GPU concurrency cap or quota-review SLA; services sleeping after inactivity do not imply account-wide fleet capacity.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Zeabur will start a new deployment using the most recent configuration.
snapshot_auto.note: Suspend (manual) and Free-plan auto-sleep ('Services on the Free Plan automatically sleep after a period of inactivity.') keep config and volumes but do not save process or root-filesystem state; resume is a fresh deployment. Automatic daily backups exist, but only for volumes/databases on Dev+ (7-day retention), and they are scheduled backups, not stop-snapshots.

egress_allowlist.quote: Outbound connections from your services are not restricted by the firewall.
egress_allowlist.note: Server firewall is inbound-only. (The Claude Code skills page loosely says 'Set inbound and outbound traffic rules for servers', but the firewall doc is explicit and no outbound feature is documented.) On a purchased server with SSH/root you could configure host iptables yourself, but that is guest-side.

egress_http_rules.quote: Outbound connections from your services are not restricted by the firewall.
egress_http_rules.note: No outbound controls of any kind, so none at HTTP level.

ingress_rules.quote: Zeabur provides server-level firewall management, allowing you to configure inbound rules directly from the Dashboard without SSH-ing into the server to manage iptables manually.
ingress_rules.note: Per-server inbound rules (TCP/UDP, port range, source IP/CIDR), default-deny ('Zeabur’s firewall uses an allowlist strategy (default-deny).'). Caveat on page: 'may still be under development or only available for certain servers'. The Gateway add-on adds IPv4 whitelist/blacklist ('Gateway supports IP-based access control to restrict who can access your services through the gateway.'). Per-service choice of which ports get domains / public host:port, plus private networking (*.zeabur.internal). No authenticated/tokenized URLs documented.

guest_firewall.quote: Zeabur provides server-level firewall management, allowing you to configure inbound rules directly from the Dashboard without SSH-ing into the server to manage iptables manually.
guest_firewall.note: Applies to Servers: full VPS (ZeaburOS=K3s, or plain Ubuntu 24.04) with SSH and sudo, so host iptables/nftables work (docs show sudo host operations). Must not block ports 22/80/443/4222/6443/30000-32767 on ZeaburOS. Inside deployed service containers, NET_ADMIN is not documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Zeabur will automatically inject these environment variables into your service.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are plain service environment variables (with ${VAR} references). No credential-injecting egress proxy documented. Zeabur AI Hub (LLM gateway) issues a key that the app itself holds.

volume_attach.quote: On Zeabur, you can mount Volumes to persistently store your data within a service.
volume_attach.note: Per-service persistent volumes (Volume ID + mount dir; billed; disables zero-downtime restarts). On Dedicated Servers you can also mount an extra disk at /var/lib/rancher/k3s/storage (host-level, via SSH). Clusters offer 'Distributed volumes that can follow workloads across nodes'.

volume_shared.quote: Volumes are scoped to a single service and cannot be shared between services.
volume_shared.note: Docs recommend network object storage (MinIO/RustFS) for shared data. Cluster distributed volumes move with a workload; they are not documented as multi-writer.
